conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.

notes: Prior (single-center referral cohort) and LRs (pooled meta-analysis) are from different sources. Terasawa's included CT studies had a pooled prevalence of about 45% (computed from Appendix Table 1 counts, p. W-100), far above 23.5%; both appear as sensitivity priors. Pickhardt's own LRs are far more extreme than the pooled LRs; we keep the pooled ones. Alvarado score as written in the note (items in data/notes/facts/B5_appy_ct.json): migration 0, anorexia 0, nausea 1, RLQ tenderness 2, rebound 0, T 37.1 0, WBC 9.4 0, left shift not reported 0; total 3. The presentation is deliberately equivocal so the 23.5% prior (all adults referred for CT) is a plausible pretest probability for the patient on the page. The Alvarado score is never stated in a note.
